dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Okay. Before you come in. Two rules.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: One, don't look at the wall for the first thirty seconds, everyone looks at the wall and then stops listening. Two, if you're going to make the face, make it now and get it over with.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (We look at the wall.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Two years of it. Printouts, photocopies, a county map with pins, and string — actual string, which she must know is a cliché and did anyway because it works.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Taki. This is a lot.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: It's eleven years of a town and I'm one person with a printer. Yes it's a lot.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: The green pins are things I've confirmed. The red are things I believe. There's forty red and nine green and I want you to notice that I keep them separate, because nobody ever notices that I keep them separate.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Nine green. Two years of work and she's willing to swear to nine things.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Nobody asks for the green ones.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Everybody asks for the wildest thing I believe so they can decide about me. You asked for the part I can prove.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Okay. Green one: the 2013 emergency response report is forty-one pages and the county holds a version that's thirty-eight. Same document number, same date, three pages fewer.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Green two: the municipal camera network doesn't legally exist. There's no procurement record, no council vote, no line item. It's just there.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Green three, and this is my favourite because it's so boring nobody's ever cared —

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: In November 2013 the town paid a marine haulage company eleven thousand dollars. The invoice says DISPOSAL — MISCELLANEOUS. That's it. That's the whole description.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Riley's hand goes to the bracelet.)

choices.choice_text: [Look at Riley first. Let her decide how much to give.]

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Tell her.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: All of it. If we're doing this we're not doing the thing where everyone gets a different half.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (So we tell her. The frames, Rowe, the cameras, the landing, the channel. It takes nine minutes and Taki doesn't interrupt once, which I suspect has never happened before in her life.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm going to need a minute. I've been right about something and it's a horrible feeling and nobody warned me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Two years I've wanted someone to say a sentence like that to me. And now you have and my first actual thought was: I wish you hadn't.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: You can walk away. Right now. Nobody would think anything.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Taki Kimura
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't be stupid. Move the green pins, I need the whole board.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Red light. Chemical smell. Sienna's the only person in this school who still shoots film and the only person who books the darkroom, which means it's hers.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: Oh — sorry, I've got it till four, I can move if you —

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: I came to find you.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She apologises before anyone's asked her to. She did it in class about the lighthouse light. I've watched her take back four true things in a year.)

choices.choice_text: "Tell me about the light again. Don't take it back this time."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: Thirty-second exposure. Tripod on the wall at the ruins. Nothing touching it, I checked, I checked twice because I knew what people would say.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: The light sweeps twice. Left, then right. And the lighthouse has been dead since 2013 so there is nothing down there to sweep.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: And I'm not going to say probably the tripod. I've said probably the tripod for two months and it isn't the tripod.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There she is.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: There's another one. The one I've never shown anybody.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: I bought a roll of film at the thrift place on Front Street in September. Used roll, undeveloped, in a bag of old junk. Two dollars. People sell them and I develop them, it's — it's a hobby, it's not weird.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: Twenty-four exposures. Twenty-three are a family barbecue in about 1998.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: Frame twenty-four is a barge at night with a crane on it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Everything stops.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: Because a picture that shouldn't exist is the kind of thing that gets you a reputation, and I already have one.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The print. Eight by ten, hanging on the line, still wet.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A barge. A crane. Floodlights. A shipping container half-lifted, dripping, being swung out over black water.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And on the deck, at the edge of the light, three men. Faces turned away. One of them in a coat that is unmistakably the coat of a man who owns things.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: There's a date on the back of the print. Whoever shot it wrote it in pencil.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: Twenty-second of November, 2013.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Taki's invoice. Eleven thousand dollars. DISPOSAL — MISCELLANEOUS. November 2013.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: It's not supernatural, is it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Sienna Morales
dialogue_sequence.text: I wanted it to be. For two months I've been hoping it was ghosts, because ghosts can't take your visa away.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He picked the meeting place. An hour out of town, in the car park of a bowling alley, which tells me everything about how frightened he is.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: Nice place. Very neutral. Very — is this where you came? After the video?

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: Oh god, it is. That's — okay, I'd like to formally note that I picked this at random and the universe is being a lot.

choices.choice_text: "It was. We had a good day."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: My mother's firm did crisis comms for Cross Industries. 2013 into 2015.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: I found the archive when I was fourteen. I was looking for money, honestly, I wanted to know how much we had. Instead I found a folder called CAULFIELD and I've had a screenshot of it on a drive for three years.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: I've never opened it in front of anyone. I've never told a person it exists. I told you, in a stairwell, because you'd just caught a three-frame cut and I thought — oh. There's someone here who looks properly.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He's got his phone out and he's not filming with it. He's holding it like it's hot.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: It's a media strategy doc. That's all it is, it's boring, it's the most boring document you've ever seen and that's what makes it —

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: It's got a section called ANTICIPATED LINES OF INQUIRY. And under it there's a list of six things a journalist might ask.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: Number four is: WHY DID THE WARNING SIRENS CEASE.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Cease. Not fail. A PR firm writing a contingency plan wrote cease, because somebody in that room knew the difference.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A four-year-old on a marina road heard it and knew the difference too.)

choices.choice_text: "Why now? Why give me this now?"

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: Because I put a laugh track on a girl being frightened and fifty-one thousand people watched it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: And I've been telling myself for two years that I'm not the bad one — Jake's the bad one, Amber's the loud one, I just edit. I just edit.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not a redemption arc. Don't put that on me. I'm not becoming a good person, I'm just tired of being efficient.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: Conditions. My mother's name never appears. Not in a paper, not in a thread, not in a conversation you have with anyone.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: She's not a criminal. She's a woman who wrote a document and cashed a cheque and she'd do it again and I still don't want her in it.

choices.choice_text: "If she's clean, she stays out. If she isn't, I'm not lying for her."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Yeah. Okay. That's more honest than what I asked for.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: One more thing and then I'm driving home and never doing this again.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: The document has a distribution list. Six names. One of them's a school principal and one of them's a chief of police.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Chase Whitmore
dialogue_sequence.text: They knew in 2013, Fiz. Not found out. Knew. They were on the distribution list.

scenes.scene_condition: Full scene requires nolan_secret_kept. If nolan_speculated instead, Nolan refuses and the scene runs short.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: You didn't say it was me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: Two weeks. Maddie Hale asked you directly, on a beach, in front of people. And you didn't say it was me.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He's been sitting on that for two weeks.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: Because it was a dirty cut and I've watched eleven thousand hours of tape and I can't unsee a dirty cut.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: That's it. It's not principle. It's a professional thing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: Anyway. I owe you, and I hate owing people, so here.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A key. Small, brass, on no keyring.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: Equipment corridor, sports block. Runs behind the library. There's a service door at the end that opens on the back of the archive.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: Card readers went on every door in September. They didn't do the service doors, because the service doors aren't on the plan anymore. The plan's from 2011.

choices.choice_text: "Nolan. If this goes wrong you're in it."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: I've had that key since sophomore year. It's where I go when I don't want to be captain of anything.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: And no. I'm not in it. I gave a kid a key to a store cupboard, that's all that happened, and if anyone asks that's what I'll say and I'll be believed, because I'm six foot four and I play for a team that Gerald Cross buys shoes for.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: That's not me being a coward. That's me telling you exactly how much protection I've got and exactly how much you haven't.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Everyone in this town knows the arithmetic of their own safety down to the decimal. Every single one of them.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: Jake's been weird, by the way. Since the frame-by-frame.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: He's not stupid. He knows somebody in this school made him look like a liar and he's been going through the list.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Nolan Burgh
dialogue_sequence.text: Watch Ezra Lang.

scenes.location: Blackwell Academy — Archive, restricted wing, 11:20 PM

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: I want to say something before we go in and I want to say it once.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: My father runs this school. If this goes wrong it doesn't go wrong for me the way it goes wrong for you. I'll get a conversation. You'll get a flight.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: So I'm going in first and I'm touching everything, and if anyone asks, I catalogued this box in September and I was re-checking my own work. Which is true. It's completely true and it's also a cover story and both of those things are fine.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Seventeen years of being the principal's daughter and she's worked out, tonight, that it's a shield she can point at other people.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Alice. That's the bravest thing anyone's said this week.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: Please don't. I'll cry and the door's on a timer.

exploration.prompt: Forty minutes before the cleaning rota reaches this corridor.

interactables.label: A shelf of yearbooks
interactables.internal_thought: (2009 through 2019. And 2013 is here. One copy, on the shelf, in the restricted archive of the school it belongs to.)
interactables.follow_up: (Four hundred were printed. Three hundred and ninety-nine went somewhere. This one's been kept — not hidden, kept. There's a difference and it matters.)

interactables.label: Open the 2013 yearbook
interactables.internal_thought: (Seniors, alphabetical. CAULFIELD, MAXINE — a girl with a fringe and a camera and a face that is trying very hard to be somewhere else.)
interactables.follow_up: (Two pages later, a photo of the yearbook committee. Third from the left, sixteen years old, unmistakable: Elena Ward.)

interactables.label: A grey archive box, catalogued in September
interactables.internal_thought: (Eighty-one prints. Alice counted them twice because that's the job.)

interactables.label: Manila folder — FACILITIES, 2013–2014
interactables.internal_thought: (Invoices. Roof repair. Boiler. Window glazing, forty-one panes.)
interactables.follow_up: (And a carbon copy of a haulage docket. NORTHWEST MARINE HAULAGE. One item. Container, 20ft, sealed. Origin: BLACKWELL ACADEMY. Destination: blank.)

interactables.label: Bound report, county letterhead
interactables.follow_up: (Taki's county copy is thirty-eight. Pages 29 to 31 are titled WARNING SYSTEM — SEQUENCE OF EVENTS.)

interactables.label: Read pages 29 to 31
interactables.internal_thought: (Timeline. 18:41 — sirens activated, all six units. 18:52 — units 1 through 4 cease. 18:53 — units 5 and 6 cease.)
interactables.follow_up: (And a line at the bottom of 31 in the flat voice of a man writing something he'd rather not: "Cessation was not consistent with progressive failure. Control-room log requested; log unavailable.")

interactables.label: The signature page
interactables.internal_thought: (Reviewed and accepted. B. DESKOWSKY, Chief of Police. H. CARTER, Blackwell Academy. And a third, in a hand that presses hard: G. CROSS.)
interactables.follow_up: (A private businessman signing off a municipal emergency review. Nobody thought that was strange enough to leave out.)

interactables.label: Bundle marked PRESCOTT — ESTATE
interactables.internal_thought: (Bankruptcy filings. The Prescott holdings went under in 2014, which everybody knows, and Taki was wrong about it being fraud, which she'll tell you herself.)
interactables.follow_up: (The distressed sale went through at four cents on the dollar to a single buyer, approved by a county board of five. Board minutes attached. One of the five is H. Carter.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
post_exploration_sequence.text: Fiz. Look at the ceiling.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (Corner of the room. Grey housing. Clean bracket.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (Five.)

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
post_exploration_sequence.text: It's not on. I checked the panel before we came in — the archive feed's been down since September.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
post_exploration_sequence.text: That's what I told myself in September, anyway. That a brand new camera was broken.

choices.choice_text: "Alice, get out. Riley and I finish this."

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
post_exploration_sequence.text: No.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
post_exploration_sequence.text: I've been getting out of rooms my whole life. I'm staying in this one.

post_exploration_sequence.speaker: Fiz
post_exploration_sequence.text: (We photograph everything. Two hundred and forty frames in thirty-one minutes and I don't stop to look at any of them.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: This is it. This is the box.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: Eighty-one prints. I catalogued it on the eleventh of September and I opened it again on the fourth of October and one of them was different.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: I've had six weeks of deciding I'm losing my mind. I would genuinely rather be losing my mind than be right.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Storm documentation. Damage assessment. Insurance photographs of a school with its roof off.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (And near the back, print sixty-something: a girl standing in the ruined west corridor, looking at the camera.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: That one.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: In September she was facing away.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The corridor's the same. The light's the same. The rubble is in exactly the same arrangement, and I mean exactly, I've spent a year learning to see this.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (But the shadow on the wall behind her is two inches further left. And her left foot is mid-step in this one and flat in my memory of Alice's description.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (This isn't the same photograph turned around. This is a different photograph, taken about a second and a half later.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Two frames. A photographer took two frames, and someone has swapped which one lives in this box.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: Oh, that's — I'm not mad. I'm not mad, I'm just not a photographer.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Why would anyone swap it? They're a second apart. They're the same picture.

choices.choice_text: "They're not. Look at the doorway behind her."
"Because in the other one, something's visible that isn't in this one."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: I scan everything. It's the job. Every print in every box gets a low-res scan for the index.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Alice Carter
dialogue_sequence.text: The September version is on the library server. It's been sitting on the library server for six weeks.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Whoever swapped the print did not know a seventeen-year-old volunteer scans everything.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's the first mistake anyone in this town has made in eleven years, and it was made by underestimating Alice Carter, which is a thing that has clearly been happening to her since birth.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: What's in the doorway, Fiz.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: In this one, nothing. A dark rectangle.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: A second and a half earlier, somebody was standing in it.

scenes.location: Blackwell Academy — Science Lab, after hours

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: You want the October 2013 data.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: Don't look surprised. Three people have asked me for it in eleven years and you all have the same face when you come through that door.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She's already got the folder out. It was already on the desk when I knocked.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: A reporter, in 2014. And Owen Rhys, about a month after he started here.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: The reporter stopped calling. Mr. Rhys made a folder and labelled it DO NOT TEACH and I've never asked him about it and he's never brought it up.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: Now. Listen carefully, because this is the part everyone gets wrong and I need you not to.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: The atmospheric data from October 2013 is strange. Pressure readings inconsistent with the observed system. Magnetic variance on the school's own instruments, three days running.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: And it is almost certainly nothing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (That's not what I came here to be told.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: The monitoring station on the ridge was installed in 1994 and last serviced in 2009. By October 2013 it was four years past its calibration window, sitting in salt air, on a mast that had been struck by lightning twice.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: I have the service records. I have the fault reports I filed in 2011 and 2012 that were never actioned because the county had no money.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: So when the numbers went strange three days before the storm, the most likely explanation is that a dying instrument died.

choices.choice_text: "Then why have you kept it for eleven years?"
"I believe you. That's not what I'm here for."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: Because a broken instrument is a boring answer and boring answers are the ones people stop checking.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: And because in eleven years nobody has ever asked me to check. Not the county, not the school, not the review. There was a forty-one page report on that storm and my data isn't in it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: That's the thing that's kept me up. Not the numbers. The fact that nobody wanted the numbers.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (This is the shape of everything here. The impossible thing has a boring answer, and the boring answer is that somebody decided you shouldn't have it.)

choices.choice_text: "Can you look at something else for me? Siren timings."
"Then let's get the numbers looked at properly."

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: Six units, all ceasing inside twelve seconds of each other, in two clean groups of four and two.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: Progressive failure is messy. Water gets into things at different rates. Four and two in twelve seconds is not water.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Ms. Valerie Leighton
dialogue_sequence.text: Four and two in twelve seconds is a person walking along a control panel.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: You've got two hundred and forty photographs of documents you weren't supposed to see, and you've brought them to a teacher at one in the morning.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: I want you to hear that sentence out loud once, from an adult, before we go any further.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: We heard it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: ...Fine. Show me the two prints.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Alice's September scan on the left. My photograph of the October print on the right.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: There. Doorway. Blow it up, don't interpolate — just crop, I want the actual pixels.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: It's a low-res index scan of a print of a negative from 2013. This is going to be four grey squares and a rumour.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (It's four grey squares and a rumour.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A person. In a doorway. Adult, tall, light-coloured coat. And that is genuinely, honestly all it is.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: I could clean it up. I could give you a face in about four hours.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: It would be a face I made. That's what enhancement is — you're not revealing information, you're asking software to invent something plausible in the gaps.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: I spent fourteen years testifying about the difference and I'm not going to be the reason you point at a man in a coat and say his name.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (He's protecting us from the exact thing he did to somebody, once. He's never going to say that out loud.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: Here's what I will tell you, and it's better than a face.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: Your eleven frames. I've had them for two weeks. The re-encode signature on those frames — the specific way that file was compressed and rewritten — I've seen it before.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: There's a batch of files that have been circulating on that anonymous board since late 2022. Photographs, mostly. All of Arcadia Bay, all supposedly historical, all with the same signature.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: Somebody has been quietly seeding forged material into this town's memory for two years and nobody has noticed because it's all been small.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Riley Jones
dialogue_sequence.text: Two years.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (2022. The year I arrived.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (The year a lot of people arrived. I'm not the only person who transferred into Blackwell in 2022 and I need to stop assuming everything is about me.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
dialogue_sequence.text: Yes. Two weeks. Because the moment I say it out loud, a seventeen-year-old goes looking for a person, and I have seen what happens when people go looking for a person.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Mr. Ethan Rowe
